Is the structure at the centre of the images a cross-section of a blood vessel or a pulmonary nodule? Answer with one word, Vessel or Nodule, then one short sentence of reasoning, then the estimated diameter in mm.

content.text:
I don't actually have access to the images in this conversation — no image data came through, so I can't make a diagnosis on this specific case.

However, here's how to make the call yourself:

**Vessel** — the central structure persists across all (or most) of the 9 slices with a similar calibre, or elongates/branches in some slices, indicating a tube running obliquely or longitudinally through the imaging plane.

**Nodule** — the structure appears, reaches a maximal round/oval cross-section on the middle slices, and disappears within the ~10 mm stack (roughly spherical), without connecting into a branching tubular pattern.

Measure the diameter on the slice where the structure is largest, using the long axis (or average of long and short axes per Fleischner guidelines).

If you can re-upload or paste the images, I'll give you the one-word answer, reasoning, and diameter estimate as requested.
